diagnosed_root_causes.closure: _revalidate_nested_locked reads PR_GET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, requires exactly 1, requires the acquisition being nested to belong to this PID, and only then is the depth incremented.  A contradiction latches debt and raises ChildSubreaperUnavailable carrying the expected and observed values, without changing the depth, the outstanding references, or the original baseline.
diagnosed_root_causes.code_path: admissible/paired_runner/process_ownership.py :: ChildSubreaperOwnership.acquire, the `if self._depth > 0 and self._applied` branch
diagnosed_root_causes.refusal_condition: A nested acquisition that increments the depth without a readback, or a contradiction that is still followed by a fork.
diagnosed_root_causes.reproduction: Acquire once against a real kernel, so depth is 1, _applied is true and PR_GET_CHILD_SUBREAPER reads 1.  Clear the process-wide flag from anywhere else in the process.  Acquire again: the previous code returned APPLIED at depth 2 without a single syscall, and PrivateMountHelper.start forked a helper whose orphaned launcher would never be reparented to this controller.
diagnosed_root_causes.violated_invariant: Every acquisition that can authorize a new helper fork must positively establish the live process-wide state immediately before it increments the ownership depth.

diagnosed_root_causes.closure: One explicit latch, stored beside the flag it describes rather than inside the object that incurred it, so replacing the ownership object -- including the module-level singleton -- inherits the debt rather than a clean slate.  It is created by each of the three failed release results, and by a refused acquisition whose rewrite of the previous value its own readback contradicts.  acquire() refuses while it stands; state(), acquire(), release() and object replacement never clear it; settle_restoration_debt() is the only operation that can, and only when the kernel reads back the owed baseline exactly.  It is PID-bound, so a fork child neither owes it nor can settle it.
diagnosed_root_causes.code_path: admissible/paired_runner/process_ownership.py :: ChildSubreaperOwnership.release, the terminal branch that recorded RESTORE_SET_FAILED, RESTORE_READBACK_FAILED or RESTORE_MISMATCH and then left depth 0 with nothing owed
diagnosed_root_causes.refusal_condition: Any acquisition granted while debt is outstanding, or any debt cleared without a positive readback of the owed baseline.
diagnosed_root_causes.reproduction: Acquire against a baseline of 0, inject a restoration mismatch on the final release, then acquire again.  The previous code read the residual kernel value 1 as a fresh baseline at the head of acquire, overwrote the original baseline, and a later release reported RESTORED to a value this process never found.
diagnosed_root_causes.violated_invariant: A failed restoration creates unresolved process-wide ownership debt.  Until it is explicitly and positively resolved, every new acquisition must refuse, no helper may fork, the original baseline must remain immutable, and no later release may convert the residual state into RESTORED.

diagnosed_root_causes.closure: An explicit helper lifecycle state machine replaces the single flag.  close() closes the protocol once, reaps the exact PID, and releases the acquisition only after a positive reap; it is idempotent once the cleanup is complete and retries the reap on every later call while it is not.  _roll_back_failed_start follows the same ordering and leaves a retryable entry rather than releasing over an unreaped child.  PrivateExecutionView.close, BoundRuntime.close and _EffectPreparation.close return and propagate the cleanup evidence, and the preparation keeps the view while its cleanup is incomplete so the retry stays reachable.
diagnosed_root_causes.code_path: admissible/paired_runner/private_workspace.py :: PrivateMountHelper.close, which set _closed on entry, released the acquisition unconditionally after a reap that may have failed, and returned immediately on every later call
diagnosed_root_causes.refusal_condition: Any ownership release without a positive reap, or a terminally non-retryable incomplete cleanup.
diagnosed_root_causes.reproduction: Stop a real helper and close it with an exhausted deadline.  The helper survives unreaped, the subreaper ownership is released anyway -- the very flag that grants the right to reap it -- the closure evidence reports the restoration complete, and a second close reports already_closed and reaps nothing.
diagnosed_root_causes.violated_invariant: Subreaper ownership may not be released until every helper process for that ownership reference is positively reaped.  Protocol closure and lifecycle completion are separate states, and an incomplete lifecycle cleanup must be retryable.

It is a delegated-cgroup result on a development host: it is neither an installed-path qualification nor an independently accepted one, and neither is claimed.

The 309-test delegated transcript of the previous closure is historical here.  It qualified the code as it stood at the starting commit and does not qualify the code this closure changed; a prior physical transcript never qualifies modified code, so this closure was qualified by its own run above.

The restoration-debt latch is deliberately sticky and process-wide: once a restoration fails verification, every acquisition in that process refuses until settle_restoration_debt reads the owed baseline back.  On a host where PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER can fail, that turns one unobserved restoration into a refusal of every later effect in the same controller process.  This is the intended fail-closed behaviour and is disclosed rather than hidden.

A poisoned ownership stays poisoned after its outstanding references are released, even when the terminal release reads the baseline back, because release() may not clear a debt.  The settlement that clears it is one non-blocking pair of syscalls and is explicit.

PrivateMountHelper.close is retryable while its cleanup is incomplete, so a caller that supplies an exhausted deadline now returns with the helper unreaped and its ownership retained rather than releasing.  A caller that never retries leaves a live child and a set process-wide flag; that outcome is reported truthfully as cleanup_complete=false rather than concealed, and the retry is one call.

A failed start whose child could not be reaped inside the rollback's deadline leaves an entry in a process-local registry so its reap and its single release stay reachable.  Nothing sweeps that registry automatically; retry_unsettled_failed_starts is called by the caller that has time to spend.

The acquisition gate remains fail-closed: a kernel that does not implement PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, or a policy that refuses it, refuses the whole effect.  This is the accepted M2-B37 behaviour and is not changed here.

While a trusted helper is alive this controller is a child subreaper.  An orphaned descendant of this controller that no effect owns would reparent here and is not reaped, because reaping it would require waitpid(-1) and could consume an unrelated child.  The window is bounded by helper lifetime and is disclosed rather than closed.

A DeprecationWarning about fork() in a multi-threaded process is emitted when the trusted mount-namespace helper is forked.  It is pre-existing, non-failing, not introduced by this closure, and is NOT closed here.
EVID-08 remains IMPLEMENTED: the retry counter belongs to the Milestone 3 cumulative budgets.
Independent acceptance and installed-path qualification are not claimed.
Milestone 3 remains forbidden and was not started.
